meta.title: TuneSync — Personal music servers, lyrics & karaoke
meta.description: Connect NAS folders, Plex, Jellyfin, Navidrome, and other personal music sources on iPhone. Play one library, enrich metadata and lyrics, and create karaoke recordings on-device.

home.headline: One app for <accent>all your private music</accent>
home.subhead: Connect WebDAV, SMB, Plex, Jellyfin, Navidrome, Synology, and more. TuneSync turns folders and media servers into one library, enriches artwork and lyrics as you listen, and transforms favorite tracks into accompaniment and recordings.
home.introTitle: From file shares to media servers, one front door is enough.
home.introBody: TuneSync unifies connection, library selection, sync, playback, and cleanup. Core metadata arrives first; artwork and analysis continue when the network is right.
home.downloadSubtitle: Connect NAS folders, Plex, Jellyfin, Navidrome, and local files on iPhone, then manage your library, lyrics, karaoke, and recordings in one place.
home.downloadIOSAria: Open the iOS getting started guide

ios.label: iOS
ios.desc: A native experience built for iPhone — connect a server, organize your library, and play.

android.label: Android
android.desc: There is no Android version today; TuneSync is currently focused on a native iPhone experience.

windows.label: Windows
windows.desc: Windows is not planned right now; the focus is on the best iPhone experience first.

quote1.text: I used to switch between several apps to play my own music. After connecting the NAS, everything is in one place.
quote1.author: Lin Yifan

quote2.text: The AI DJ's auto-continue is genuinely useful — it tops up the queue when it runs low, so I don't have to keep selecting.
quote2.author: M. Chen

quote3.text: I didn't expect to remove vocals and sing on my phone. Drop the vocal, sing with the accompaniment, and play it back afterward.
quote3.author: Kai

quote4.text: My library info was fairly disorganized. After one batch organize, the artwork and release years are mostly filled in.
quote4.author: Zhang Rui

quote5.text: I appreciate using my own API key — requests go straight to the model I chose, without any intermediary.
quote5.author: D. Wang

quote6.text: It found my server on the LAN automatically and connected after a quick setup — easier than I expected.
quote6.author: Eric

home.ctaTitle: Choose a source. Bring the whole library.
home.ctaBody: Connect a folder or media server, choose its music library, and start syncing and listening.

features.title: Features
features.subtitle: Multi-source library, progressive metadata, playback, lyrics, karaoke, and recording polish — together in one app.

library.title: Library
library.desc: Connect file shares, NAS devices, and popular self-hosted media servers as one library.
library.featureTitle: Bring folders and media servers into one library
library.featureDesc: TuneSync can index WebDAV, SMB, FTP, NFS, and Synology DSM folders, or sync the structured music libraries already managed by Plex, Jellyfin, Emby, Navidrome, Subsonic, and Audio Station. Different sources, one browsing and playback experience.
library.featureB1: Local / WebDAV / FTP / SMB / NFS / Synology DSM
library.featureB2: Plex / Jellyfin / Emby / Navidrome / Subsonic / Audio Station
library.featureB3: Unified library selection, paged sync, stable track IDs, and incremental refresh
library.featureB4: Direct play, plus server transcoding and artwork where supported

player.title: Playback
player.desc: Full-screen player with line-by-line synced lyrics, queue, sleep timer, AirPlay.
player.featureTitle: Lyrics highlight line by line as the song plays
player.featureDesc: The player scrolls lyrics in time with playback and highlights the current line — tap any line to jump there. The background color is sampled from the artwork, and you can switch to plain-text reading mode when no timing is available.

karaoke.title: Sing along
karaoke.desc: Separate vocals and accompaniment on-device, lower the original vocal, and record yourself with the microphone.
karaoke.featureTitle: Remove the vocal, sing with the accompaniment
karaoke.featureDesc: TuneSync splits a track into vocal and accompaniment stems on your device, with independent volume for each. Lower the original vocal, keep the accompaniment, and sing along — the microphone records your performance in sync. The first separation takes a moment; results are cached for reuse.
karaoke.featureB2: Live vocal-level control with a 3-2-1 countdown
karaoke.featureB3: Mic recording with input/output latency compensation
karaoke.featureB4: Saves to “My Recordings” with a direct path into Recording Studio

recordingStudio.title: Recording Studio
recordingStudio.desc: See the real waveform, trim and shape your karaoke recordings, and save without touching the original.
recordingStudio.featureTitle: Polish a take into the version worth keeping
recordingStudio.featureDesc: After saving a karaoke take, open it directly in Recording Studio. Select the keep range on its real waveform, adjust master volume, and add Studio or Concert Hall ambience. The original stays intact for instant comparison, undo, or restoration.
recordingStudio.featureB1: Real waveform timeline with precise trim handles
recordingStudio.featureB2: Master volume plus Studio and Concert Hall ambience
recordingStudio.featureB3: Original / Edited A/B preview with undo and redo
recordingStudio.featureB4: Non-destructive save, share, and one-tap restore

ai.title: AI assistant
ai.desc: Bring your own API key. Let AI pick the next song or tidy up file names.
ai.featureTitle: Use your own key with your preferred model
ai.featureDesc: Enter your own API key to get started — OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Zhipu, DeepSeek and others are preconfigured, or specify a custom endpoint or local Ollama. The AI DJ continues your queue based on your listening habits, and can tidy up irregular file names.
ai.featureB2: Instant / reasoning model roles, auto-selected per task
ai.featureB3: AI DJ with three autonomy levels: preview / one-tap / auto-continue
ai.featureB4: Tool calling: web search, album art, lyrics, playback and playlist control

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.desc: Use core metadata immediately, then enrich artwork, release data, and audio analysis in the background.
metadata.featureTitle: Use the library now. Let the details finish behind it.
metadata.featureDesc: Titles, artists, and albums supplied by a remote source appear immediately. Missing release data, artwork, AI assistance, BPM, and audio analysis enter a durable enhancement queue. TuneSync automatically scales work for Wi-Fi, cellular, and Low Data Mode.
metadata.featureB2: Full enrichment on Wi-Fi; lightweight lookups on cellular and Low Data Mode
metadata.featureB3: Durable queues that retry, cancel safely, and resume after relaunch
metadata.featureB4: Manual fields stay protected with source and change history

discovery.title: Discover
discovery.desc: See charts from Apple Music / Bilibili / YouTube, identify songs with ShazamKit.
discovery.featureTitle: When you're not sure what to play
discovery.featureDesc: Home aggregates charts from several platforms. When you don't have a specific track in mind, TuneSync offers recommendations based on your listening history. Hear a song you like? Open recognition to identify it.
discovery.featureB1: Apple Music / Bilibili / YouTube / Last.fm multi-source charts
discovery.featureB2: Suggestions based on what you usually play

intro.title: TuneSync docs
intro.lead: From first sync to the full technical specification.
intro.body: The docs follow the real workflow: choose a source, sync and organize, play and follow lyrics, sing and record, then configure AI and system behavior. Start with Getting started. For compatibility, network policy, security, and implementation boundaries, read Technical specification.

technical.title: TuneSync technical specification
technical.lead: Implementation boundaries for deployment, compatibility review, and advanced use.

current.title: Current baseline
current.body: This page describes TuneSync 1.0.10 (Build 36), based on the main project and an iPhone 17 Simulator build verified on August 10, 2026.

app.v: Native iPhone app with a Live Activity extension

stack.v: SwiftUI, Observation, Swift 6 concurrency, and async/await

persistence.v: SwiftData library and task state, filesystem caches, and Keychain credentials

extensions.v: ActivityKit, App Intents, Shortcuts, Siri, Spotlight, AirPlay, and background audio

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.body: TuneSync separates UI, source adapters, synchronization, metadata, playback, and audio processing, connecting different servers through a unified track descriptor and playback resource.
architecture.ui: SwiftUI renders the interface; shared state uses Observation and updates on the main actor.
architecture.sources: A unified client capability model exposes library selection, pagination, stable IDs, direct play, download, transcoding, and artwork per source.
architecture.tasks: Indexing, metadata enrichment, artwork, BPM, and vocal separation run as cancellable async work; durable queues resume after relaunch.
architecture.playback: AVFoundation plays local or remote resources; sources may provide authenticated direct-play or server-transcoded URLs.

files.v: Local folders, WebDAV/WebDAVs, FTP/FTPS, SMB, NFS, and Synology DSM

servers.v: Plex, Jellyfin, Emby, Navidrome, Subsonic/OpenSubsonic, and Synology Audio Station

selection.v: Folders for file sources; music libraries or collections for media servers

delivery.v: Direct play first; transcoding, pagination, remote artwork, and downloads when declared by the source

metadata.title: Metadata pipeline
metadata.body: Synchronization separates library readiness from full enrichment so large remote libraries are not blocked by artwork or analysis.
metadata.core: Title, artist, album, duration, and server-provided artwork locators are written first to complete the core sync.
metadata.enrichment: Release information, high-resolution artwork, AI assistance, BPM, and audio features are queued as independent enhancements.
metadata.budget: Offline pauses work; cellular or Low Data Mode permits lightweight catalog lookups; Wi-Fi or Ethernet enables artwork, AI, remote media reads, and audio analysis.
metadata.provenance: Fields retain source and history; automatic enrichment never overwrites a manual edit.

security.title: Security and privacy
security.credentials: Server passwords, device tokens, and AI API keys are stored in the system Keychain rather than the library database.
security.transport: Use HTTPS, a VPN, or a securely configured reverse proxy for remote access. LAN discovery is limited to the current local network.
security.diagnostics: Locally generated diagnostic reports exclude passwords and API keys; credential fields remain masked in UI and test evidence.
security.ai: Bring-your-own-key requests go directly to the selected provider or self-hosted endpoint. AI features are optional.

audio.title: Audio, karaoke, and recording
audio.body: Playback, mixing, and recording use AVFoundation. Vocal separation and parts of the lyrics workflow run on-device.
audio.formats: Playback supports MP3, FLAC, WAV, AAC, M4A, AIFF, and Opus; final compatibility still depends on iOS decoding and the server's delivery format.
audio.separation: Core ML MDX / DTTNet pipelines split a track into vocal and accompaniment stems and cache reusable results.
audio.recording: Recording Studio stores trim, gain, EQ, reverb, and render state non-destructively while retaining the original take.

system.title: Background and system capabilities
system.body: TuneSync supports background audio, lock-screen now playing, queues, AirPlay, and sleep timers. Indexing, metadata, and separation can surface task state and Live Activities, while App Intents expose playback and recognition actions.

limits.title: Boundaries and dependencies
limits.body: Actual server capabilities, transcoding formats, and authentication methods depend on the server version and configuration. Remote reliability depends on network, certificates, and server performance. Separation, recording, and speech recognition require supported device resources and system permissions.

gettingStarted.title: Getting started
gettingStarted.lead: Choose a file source or media server and complete the first library sync in four steps.
gettingStarted.shotHint: Replace with a real screenshot: public/screenshots/getting-started.png

overview.title: The overall flow
overview.body: First launch introduces source connection, sync scope, library creation, and later enrichment. The unified Library Sources & Indexing page shows servers, folders, local and remote track counts, and brings refresh, selection, and indexing status together.

step1.title: Welcome
step1.body: A quick intro to what TuneSync does: wires your servers, folders, and player together.

step2.title: Connect servers
step2.body: Choose WebDAV, SMB, NFS, FTP, or Synology DSM for file-based sources. Choose Plex, Jellyfin, Emby, Navidrome, Subsonic, or Audio Station for media servers. Enter the address, sign in, or authorize the account as requested.

step3.title: Add your library
step3.body: For file sources, select only the folders to index. For media servers, select a music library or collection. Browse and play as soon as core metadata arrives; artwork, release data, and analysis continue in the background.

step4.title: Polish
step4.body: Artwork, lyrics, karaoke. Tap a karaoke-ready track to enter sing mode — lyrics scroll on their own, drop the vocal as low as you like, works on the lock screen and in the background.

tip.title: See it again
tip.body: Settings → User Guide reopens the tour; Settings → Setup Guide maintains a checklist of remaining steps to complete.

permissions.title: Permissions you'll be asked for
permissions.body: Only when you use the thing that needs it:
permissions.localNetwork: Local network — to discover LAN WebDAV, FTP, SMB, NFS, NAS, and media servers
permissions.microphone: Microphone — used for song recognition (identifying music playing nearby) and karaoke recording
permissions.speech: Speech recognition — transcribes the vocal on-device to add timing to plain lyrics
permissions.applemusic: Apple Music — so playback can continue in the background

next.title: Up next
next.body: Ready to connect a server? Read on in “Library”.

library.title: Library
library.lead: Combine local folders, network shares, and self-hosted media servers into a single library.
library.shotHint: Replace with a real screenshot: public/screenshots/library.png

protocols.title: File-based sources
protocols.body: Browse and index by directory, ideal for NAS shares and general file servers:
protocols.webdav: WebDAV — the most common for self-hosting; also supports encrypted WebDAVs
protocols.smb: SMB — Windows sharing and most NAS defaults; common for Synology, QNAP, etc.
protocols.nfs: NFS — common network filesystem on Linux and NAS, fast
protocols.ftp: FTP / FTPS — classic file transfer; FTPS is the encrypted variant
protocols.synology: Browse shared folders through Synology Web APIs with DSM login and two-factor authentication flows

mediaServers.title: Structured media servers
mediaServers.body: Sync the server's existing library structure, metadata, and artwork instead of re-parsing every item as a generic file:
mediaServers.plex: Plex account authorization, server selection, music-library sync, direct play, and server transcoding
mediaServers.mediaBrowser: Jellyfin and Emby share a MediaBrowser adapter with pagination, artwork, and stable track IDs
mediaServers.openSubsonic: Navidrome and Subsonic/OpenSubsonic support library selection, pagination, direct play, transcoding, and artwork
mediaServers.audioStation: Synology Audio Station API syncs music and artwork and generates authenticated playback URLs

step1.title: Open library sources
step1.body: Under “Settings → Library Sources & Indexing”, tap “Add Server”, or go in from the Home “Connect a Server” prompt.

step2.title: Pick a protocol, enter the address
step2.body: Choose a file protocol or media server. File sources use address, port, and path; media servers guide you through sign-in, quick connect, or account authorization.

step3.title: Enter credentials, save
step3.body: Test the connection, then select a folder, music library, or collection. Credentials and device tokens are stored in the system Keychain.

step4.title: Pick folders to index
step4.body: Submit the selection to sync. Browse and play once core metadata is ready; artwork and analysis continue in the background according to network conditions.

discover.title: Bonjour auto-discovery
discover.body: On the same network, TuneSync discovers WebDAV, SMB, FTP, and NFS services. Some media servers also support quick connect or account authorization. For internet access, use HTTPS, a VPN, or a securely configured reverse proxy.

indexing.title: Indexing
indexing.body: File sources scan selected folders and read audio tags; media servers page through structured tracks, albums, and artwork locators. Both map into the same TuneSync library model. Core metadata is written first and enhancements are queued later, so large remote libraries do not wait on every cover or analysis job.
indexing.note: Sync stays within the folders, music libraries, or collections you selected. Later refreshes use stable IDs, revisions, and modified dates for incremental updates, with progress and results visible in Background Tasks.

playlists.title: Playlists and favorites
playlists.favorite: Favorite a track — favorites show up on Home and in the favorites list

player.title: Player
player.lead: Full-screen player, mini player, queue, and playback controls.
player.shotHint: Replace with a real screenshot: public/screenshots/player-lyrics.png

modes.title: Three modes
modes.body: The full-screen player switches between three views at the bottom — tap to change:
modes.normal: Standard — big artwork, track title and artist, scrubber, playback controls. The background gradient is pulled from the artwork, so it's different for every track.
modes.lyrics: Lyrics — scroll line by line in time with the song, current line highlighted. Tracks without timing fall back to reading mode (plain text).
modes.queue: Queue — view and reorder upcoming tracks.

controls.title: Playback controls
controls.scrub: Drag the scrubber to any second — let go to seek
controls.shuffle: Shuffle and repeat (off / list / single track)
controls.speed: Playback speed (0.75x / 1x / 1.25x / 1.5x / 2x) — useful for practicing a song or skimming
controls.airplay: AirPlay to a HomePod, Apple TV, or other AirPlay device

menu.title: Top menu
menu.body: The full-screen player's top menu has:
menu.importLrc: Import LRC — pick a lyrics file, reads the timing and applies instantly
menu.searchLyrics: Search lyrics — from LRCLIB / Genius / Musixmatch
menu.generateLyrics: Generate synced lyrics — when you only have plain text, let AI figure out the timing on-device
menu.searchMetadata: Search metadata — find artwork and release info for the current track
menu.aiDj: AI DJ — let AI queue songs based on your taste
menu.sleep: Sleep timer — auto-stops after 15 min to 1 hour

queue.title: Play queue
queue.body: The queue lists upcoming tracks. Tap a track to play it now, swipe to remove, or clear all (it asks for confirmation). When empty, it prompts you to add tracks from the library. Adding a track can be set to play next or append to the end.

bg.title: Background and lock screen
bg.body: TuneSync declares a background audio entitlement, so playback continues on the lock screen and in the background. The lock screen, Control Center, and Dynamic Island all control playback and show lyrics — no need to switch back to the app.

lyrics.title: Lyrics
lyrics.lead: Line-by-line synced lyrics, reading mode, and multi-source lyric retrieval.
lyrics.shotHint: Replace with a real screenshot: public/screenshots/lyrics.png

modes.title: Two modes
modes.body: The lyrics view switches automatically based on whether timing exists:
modes.synced: Synced: aligned to playback, current line highlighted, auto-scroll. Tap a line to jump there; drag up or down to browse (it resumes following the current position after a moment). Gradient masks fade the top and bottom edges. Animations are driven by a dedicated motion engine, with a fullscreen background that breathes through the artwork's color. Honors the system Reduce Motion setting.
modes.reading: Reading: just plain-text lyrics, no timing. Good when you want to read without the scroll.

sources.title: Where lyrics come from
sources.body: TuneSync tries lyrics sources in this order and stops at the first hit:
sources.lrclib: LRCLIB — open synced-lyrics database. Exact match first (artist + title + duration), then a fuzzy search. The most common source; free, no key.
sources.genius: Genius — found by search, then parsed from the page HTML. Usually plain text, may need timing generated.
sources.musixmatch: Musixmatch — comprehensive, but needs your own API key (set under Settings → Metadata & Lyrics).

sidecar.v: a .lrc or .txt beside the audio file — lyrics that came with your import

webdav.v: a .lrc / .txt beside the audio on the server, pulled over WebDAV

import.title: Import LRC
import.body: From the player's top menu, pick Import LRC and choose a .lrc file. It reads the timing tags and applies immediately — that track uses this lyrics file from now on. You can also import plain-text .txt, but that only enters reading mode.

generate.title: Generate synced lyrics
generate.body: Only have plain text and want line sync? Pick Generate Synced Lyrics from the top menu. TuneSync listens on-device for when the vocal happens in the song, then aligns it with the text. It tells you its confidence along the way, and the result is stored on the track so it's not recomputed.

confidence.title: About “confidence”
confidence.body: AI-aligned lyrics include a confidence score (0–100%). When it is low (for example, below 60%) a warning appears and you can retry. Confidence depends on whether a clear vocal is present and how well the text lines map to the detected timing. If the result is unsatisfactory, edit the LRC and re-import to overwrite.

tuning.title: Lyrics display
tuning.body: In Settings you can tweak how lyrics look:
tuning.size: Font size — bigger to read easily, smaller to fit more lines on screen
tuning.spacing: Line spacing — how much room between lines
tuning.motion: Motion — honors the system Reduce Motion setting; on means less scrolling animation

karaoke.title: Karaoke
karaoke.lead: Separate vocals and accompaniment on-device, lower the original vocal, and record yourself with the microphone.
karaoke.shotHint: Replace with a real screenshot: public/screenshots/karaoke.png

how.title: How it works
how.body: In karaoke mode, TuneSync splits the song into vocal and accompaniment stems right on your phone, and the two volumes are independent: drop the original vocal, keep the accompaniment, and sing along. The whole thing runs on-device — your songs aren't uploaded and it doesn't hit the network.

step1.title: Prepare the split
step1.body: In the player, tap the mic button and pick “Prepare Karaoke”. TuneSync splits the song into vocal and accompaniment on-device, processes it in chunks, and caches the result for next time.

step2.title: Start
step2.body: When it's ready the button becomes “Start Karaoke”. Tap it — the accompaniment plays, vocal dropped.

step3.title: Adjust the vocal, record
step3.body: Use the vertical slider to set how much vocal stays. Want to record? Tap record, count down 3-2-1, and it captures your voice mixed with the accompaniment.

step4.title: Save, play back
step4.body: On stop you can “Save and Stop”, “Discard”, or “Keep going”. Saved recordings live in “Settings → My Recordings” — play, share, or clear them.

balance.title: Vocal slider
balance.body: The karaoke console has a vertical slider: push up to raise the original vocal, push to the top to collapse it back into the mic button. After the split finishes it pops open with a little haptic. Drag to the bottom to fully mute the vocal, or stop halfway to leave a little for guidance.

record.title: Recording
record.body: Tap record to start; the full flow:
record.countdown: 3-2-1 Get ready countdown — time to put on headphones, find the key
record.meter: Live input level (green → yellow → red) and a timer while recording, so you can see how loud you are and how long you've been singing
record.pause: Pause and resume, in sync with playback — pause the song and recording stops too
record.save: On stop: Save and Stop, Discard Recording, or Keep going — no accidental deletes

model.title: First time needs a model
model.body: Vocal separation uses an on-device model (MDX-light, running via Core ML). First use means getting it ready under Settings → Vocal Separation — just download it. Separation works in chunks stitched together (chunk + overlap-add), and the result is cached for reuse — so the first time a given song takes a bit (tens of seconds), after that it's instant.

recordings.title: My Recordings
recordings.body: Saved takes live in Settings → My Recordings as .m4a files. Play, share, or delete them, or open Recording Studio to trim and shape the sound. A take contains your vocal and accompaniment with input/output latency compensation to keep them aligned.

studio.title: Keep editing after you save
studio.body: After Save and Stop, choose Edit Recording to enter Recording Studio immediately. You can also open it later from Settings → My Recordings. Edits render to a separate file, so the original take is never overwritten.

compatibility.title: Karaoke device compatibility
compatibility.body: TuneSync requires iOS 18 or later. iPhone 13 and newer support full automatic vocal separation; iPhone 12 can prepare individual songs manually. iPhone 11 and earlier cannot create new separations, but cached karaoke tracks and existing recordings remain available.

live.title: Live Activity
live.body: Separation supports Live Activity — the Dynamic Island and lock screen show how far along the split is, so you don't have to stay in the app and wait.

recordingStudio.title: Recording Studio
recordingStudio.lead: Trim karaoke takes against their real waveform, shape the sound, and keep an original you can always restore.

open.title: How to open it
open.body: After saving a karaoke take, choose Edit Recording. Or go to Settings → My Recordings, open a recording's menu, and choose edit.

step1.title: Choose the keep range on the waveform
step1.body: Drag the trim handles at either end of the timeline, or park the playhead and set it as the start or end. The final duration updates as you work.

step2.title: Compare the original and edit
step2.body: Switch between Original and Edited, then use play, skip back or forward five seconds, and the timeline to check every cut and sound change.

step3.title: Shape the sound
step3.body: Open Sound to adjust the master level and choose No Ambience, Studio, or Concert Hall room character.

step4.title: Save or share
step4.body: Tap Save to render the edited version. Share the finished file directly, or restore the original from the More menu when you want a clean start.

controls.title: Editing controls
controls.timeline: The waveform timeline shows the selected range, playhead, and final duration
controls.preview: Original / Edited A/B preview with five-second skip controls
controls.history: Undo and redo track trim and sound changes made in the current editing session
controls.share: Sharing uses the current effective version; save first to share the finished edit

nondestructive.title: Non-destructive by design
nondestructive.body: Saving an edit never overwrites the original .m4a. TuneSync keeps the source and renders a separate edited copy, so you can revise it again or restore the original with one action.

format.title: Files and storage
format.body: Original and edited recordings stay in the app's local storage. The list marks edited takes and shows effective duration and total stored size; deleting a recording removes both its source and edited file.

ai.title: AI assistant
ai.lead: Use your own API key to let AI recommend tracks, tidy file names, or write album intros. Requests go directly to your chosen provider, without an intermediary.
ai.shotHint: Replace with a real screenshot: public/screenshots/ai-dj.png

step1.title: Turn it on
step1.body: Under “Settings → Metadata & Lyrics → AI Assistance”, flip on “AI Assistance”.

step2.title: Pick a provider
step2.body: Under Connection choose one — OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Zhipu, DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen and others are preset, or enter a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint or local Ollama. Then the Base URL (presets fill it in automatically).

step3.title: Enter key and model
step3.body: Paste your API key (secure input), then pick a fast model (for recommendations, filename cleanup) and a reasoning model (for things like album intros that need thinking). You can type a model name, or tap Available Models to pick from the list pulled from your provider.

step4.title: Test it
step4.body: Tap “Test Connection” to see if it works, or send a message in “AI Trial Chat” — if it replies, you're set.

roles.title: Two models
roles.body: TuneSync has two model roles, picked automatically by task — no manual switching:

instant.v: Quick and cheap — AI DJ recommendations, filename cleanup, quick Q&A; replies in seconds

reasoning.v: Slower, higher quality — for things like album intros that need some thought; you can set how hard it thinks (minimal/low/medium/high). Also supports reasoning-model-specific adaptive thinking.

dj.title: AI DJ
dj.body: The AI DJ queues songs based on what you play, skip, and favorite. Three autonomy levels:
dj.preview: Preview before play — show recommendations, you choose what to play
dj.oneTap: One-tap play — confirm and it starts
dj.auto: Automatic continuation — tops up the queue itself when it's running low, hands-off

tools.title: Tool calling
tools.body: When Tool calling is on, the model can use these tools (read-only ones are always allowed; read-write ones need your OK):
tools.web: web_search — search the web via DuckDuckGo (album background, artist info)
tools.fetch: fetch_webpage — pull a specific page's content for closer reading
tools.art: search_album_art — find artwork, upscale small images to 1200x1200
tools.library: search_library — search songs within your library
tools.custom: Custom tools — tools you define, letting the model call your own endpoints

privacy.title: On privacy
privacy.body: AI calls use your own key and go straight to your chosen provider — TuneSync's servers don't handle them. Turn on tool calling and smart tool selection as needed: keep the capability while controlling cost. Any AI feature can be switched off in settings at any time.

trial.title: Trial chat
trial.body: A trial chat is available under AI Assistance — send a message without opening a specific feature to verify the connection works and the model responds. After configuring your key, it is recommended to test here first.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.lead: Use core metadata first, then progressively enrich artwork, release data, lyrics, and audio analysis according to network and scraping mode.
metadata.shotHint: Replace with a real screenshot: public/screenshots/metadata.png

modes.title: Three scraping modes
modes.body: The mode decides whether source metadata is accepted immediately or followed by external catalog lookups, and which enhancements are queued.

fast.v: Accept source core metadata and skip additional enrichment; best for a server that is already well organized

balanced.v: Accept complete core metadata immediately and fill only missing release information and available artwork

precise.v: Continue multi-source lookup and queue release data, artwork, AI assistance, and audio analysis

progressive.title: Progressive enrichment
progressive.body: TuneSync separates core synchronization from independent enhancement work so large libraries are not blocked by artwork or audio analysis.
progressive.core: Title, artist, album, duration, and other core fields enter the library first and are immediately playable
progressive.deferred: Artwork, release data, AI mood features, BPM, and audio analysis queue and retry independently
progressive.network: Cellular and Low Data Mode use lightweight catalog lookups; Wi-Fi or Ethernet restores full enrichment
progressive.resume: Enhancement state is durable and resumes after cancellation, temporary failure, or relaunch

manualProtection.title: Manual fields come first
manualProtection.body: Automatic enrichment never overwrites titles, artists, albums, years, artwork, BPM, or other fields you edited manually. Source and change history remain available for review and rollback.

sources.title: Sources
sources.body: TuneSync pulls info from these sources, then compares and picks the best:
sources.itunes: iTunes — artwork, release year, copyright, album tracklist; artwork up to 1200x1200. Highest match quality.
sources.musicbrainz: MusicBrainz — open metadata with stable track IDs, useful for cross-referencing other databases.
sources.ai: AI — uses your configured model to clean filenames and guess missing fields (e.g. fixing a misspelled title).

embedded.v: tags already in the audio file (ID3 / FLAC tags) — read first during indexing

single.title: Refresh one track
single.body: From a track's detail page or the player's top menu, pick Search Metadata. The app lists candidates, each scored by match quality (does the title, artist, album, duration line up?). Pick one, choose which fields to write, and it writes back. Every field change records who provided it. Want to manually correct a field? Tracks have an inline edit card — tap any field (title, artist, album, year, genre) to overwrite it; manual edits are tagged as such in Metadata History.

album.title: A whole album
album.body: The album detail page can refresh the whole album at once — no need to go track by track:
album.tracklist: Match the full tracklist — multi-disc included, disc and track numbers line up
album.missing: Flag tracks that are Missing from library — indicates which tracks from the album you have not yet collected
album.intro: Have AI write an album intro — verifies the album's background on the web first, streams the text as it writes, with a confidence score

artist.title: A single artist
artist.body: The artist detail page refreshes the artist — bio, image, MusicBrainz / Wikidata / Wikipedia IDs. Once refreshed it applies to all that artist's tracks automatically, so you don't edit them one by one.

weights.title: Source weights
weights.body: Under Settings → Metadata & Lyrics set source weights and per-field overwrite rules. When sources disagree, your weights decide who wins; and whether to overwrite existing values. For example: prefer iTunes for artwork, but trust embedded tags for the title.

batch.title: Batch organize
batch.body: Whole-library organizing reports core scraping and enhancement work separately. Background Tasks shows completed, pending, failed, and remaining enhancement counts. Stop the current batch, retry failed items independently, or let artwork, AI, BPM, and audio analysis continue when Wi-Fi returns.

history.title: History and rollback
history.body: Every refresh records who provided each field, what the value was before, and what it became. You can review it in Metadata History and revert if you don't like it.

discovery.title: Discover
discovery.lead: Home recommendations, multi-platform charts, and song recognition to help you find what to play next.
discovery.shotHint: Replace with a real screenshot: public/screenshots/discovery.png

home.title: Home
home.body: Home arranges sections based on your library contents and listening habits — empty sections are hidden:
home.foryou: For You — a recommendation playlist computed from your taste, refreshed each visit
home.most: Most Played — the tracks you loop the most
home.recent: Continue Listening / Recently Added — pick up where you left off, or see what just landed
home.genres: Browse by Genre — rock, electronic, classical, etc.

trends.title: Multi-platform charts
trends.body: After enabling chart sources under Settings → Home & Discovery, Home shows these platforms' charts, ranked:

foryou.title: For You
foryou.body: For You puts out a main pick (a collage of a few tracks' artwork) plus secondary picks, each with a reason and a Preview Mix — tap to preview, and add to the queue if you like it.

feedback.title: Feedback tuning
feedback.body: Not loving a pick? From the full-screen player's menu, tell the AI DJ — like or less of this. The app remembers and steers future recommendations toward what you like.

recognize.title: Recognition
recognize.body: Hear a good song at a café or shop? Open Recognition and TuneSync uses ShazamKit to listen for a few seconds and tell you what it is. Recognized songs are kept — browse them under Settings → Song Recognition, and add favorites straight to your library.

settings.title: Settings
settings.lead: Appearance, language, player animation, cache, and background tasks.
settings.shotHint: Replace with a real screenshot: public/screenshots/settings.png

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.body: Theme and language follow the system by default, or set them explicitly. Changes apply immediately — no restart.

animation.title: Player animation
animation.body: Tune the player animations if they feel like too much or too little:
animation.height: Mini-player height — how much room it takes at the bottom
animation.ramp: Backdrop ramp — how strongly the artwork color fills the background
animation.delay: Controls reveal — the timing of buttons appearing when you enter full-screen

cache.title: Cache and storage
cache.body: Under Settings → Cache & Storage, see how much artwork, audio, and temp cache take up. If it's gotten large, clear it in one tap. Clearing doesn't touch your library — next time you browse it just regenerates thumbnails and caches.

tasks.title: Background tasks and logs
tasks.body: Settings → Background Tasks & Logs puts progress, cancellable tasks, and failure reasons for four task types in one place. While a task runs, the home screen shows a progress banner too:
tasks.indexing: Library indexing — scanning folders, reading embedded info, building the library
tasks.metadata: Metadata scraping — filling in info from iTunes / MusicBrainz / AI
tasks.separation: Vocal separation — splitting a track into vocal + accompaniment (for karaoke)
tasks.lyrics: Synced lyrics alignment — adding timing to plain lyrics

guide.title: User guide
guide.body: Settings → User Guide reopens the first-launch tour; Settings → Setup Guide maintains a checklist of remaining steps to complete.

intents.title: Siri, Shortcuts & Spotlight
intents.body: TuneSync exposes two App Intents to the system — Play Track and Start Karaoke. They appear in the Shortcuts app, can be triggered by Siri (try “Hey Siri, play my music”), and are searchable in Spotlight. Use them to kick off playback or jump straight into karaoke without opening the app.

about.title: About
about.body: Settings → About TuneSync — version number, whether the separation model is ready, and third-party library credits.

plus.title: TuneSync Plus
plus.lead: An optional subscription for advanced audio, lyrics, metadata, and discovery features. Core listening stays free.

overview.title: What Plus unlocks
overview.body: TuneSync Plus unlocks the advanced capabilities below. Some compute-heavy features also include a recurring free allowance:

features.title: Included with Plus
features.separation: Vocal separation (Karaoke) — split a track into vocal and accompaniment on-device
features.lyrics: Synced lyrics generation — let the app add timing to plain-text lyrics on-device
features.scraping: Precise metadata scraping — slowest, most thorough scraping mode that checks every source
features.trends: Apple Music Trend Discovery — the current region's Top 10

free.title: What's free
free.body: Core listening stays free: local folders, WebDAV / SMB / NFS / FTP / Synology DSM, plus Plex, Jellyfin, Emby, Navidrome, Subsonic, and Audio Station; library sync, background playback, existing synchronized lyrics, recognition, and basic metadata organization are included. Vocal separation and synced-lyrics generation share two free uses per week; BPM and audio-feature analysis includes five per day. The app shows current allowances and device eligibility.

purchase.title: Purchasing
purchase.body: Plus is a recurring subscription billed by Apple through the App Store. Regional pricing is shown on the subscribe screen inside the app. Apple handles the transaction; TuneSync only learns whether you have an active entitlement — we never see your payment details.

manage.title: Manage or cancel
manage.body: You can manage or cancel anytime in System Settings → Apple ID → Subscriptions. Cancellation stops renewal at the end of the current billing period; access stays until then.

privacy.title: On privacy
privacy.body: Subscriptions are processed entirely by Apple's StoreKit. We do not collect or store payment information, full receipt data, or your Apple ID. The only thing we read is a boolean entitlement state — whether Plus is currently active.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: TuneSync is designed with privacy as a core principle. This policy explains what data we collect and how we use it.

noCollection.title: Data We Do Not Collect
noCollection.body: TuneSync is a local-first music player. We do not collect, store, or transmit your personal data to our servers. Specifically:
noCollection.p1: We do not require an account or login.
noCollection.p2: We do not track your listening habits or activity.
noCollection.p3: We do not sell or share your data with third parties.

onDevice.title: Data Stored on Your Device
onDevice.body: The following data is stored on your device and is not sent to TuneSync-owned servers. When you intentionally use metadata, lyrics, or AI services, the relevant query is sent directly to the provider you selected:
onDevice.p1: Your music library index (song titles, artists, album names, file paths).
onDevice.p2: Album artwork and metadata fetched for your songs.
onDevice.p3: Lyrics downloaded or generated for display during playback.
onDevice.p4: Karaoke recordings you create (stored only if you choose to save them).
onDevice.footer: You can remove caches, recordings, and sources inside the app, or delete the library stored in the app container. Removing a source also removes the secure credentials associated with that source.

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.mic: Microphone: Used for song recognition and karaoke recording, and requested only when you enter those features. Saved takes remain on your device.
permissions.speech: Speech Recognition: Used to transcribe vocals on-device and add timing to plain-text lyrics.
permissions.network: Local Network: Used to discover and connect to WebDAV, SMB, FTP, NFS, NAS devices, and media servers on the current LAN.
permissions.music: Apple Music: Used to import artwork and metadata from your Apple Music library if you choose to use that feature.

ai.title: Optional AI Features
ai.body: TuneSync may use on-device machine learning or an optional AI provider (configured by you in Settings) to fetch metadata, album art, and lyrics. If you enable a third-party AI provider, data about your songs (title, artist, album) may be sent to that provider's API. This is entirely optional and disabled by default.

subscriptions.title: Subscriptions
subscriptions.body: TuneSync offers an optional TuneSync Plus subscription that unlocks vocal separation, synced lyrics generation, precise metadata scraping, and trend discovery. Purchases are processed entirely by Apple's App Store via StoreKit. We never see, store, or process your payment information — Apple only tells us whether you have an active entitlement. You can manage or cancel your subscription at any time in System Settings → Apple ID → Subscriptions.

webdav.title: Remote source credentials
webdav.body: Server passwords, device tokens, and AI API keys are stored in the device Keychain and used only with sources or providers you configure. They are not written to the library database or local diagnostic reports. TuneSync does not operate a server that proxies these credentials or your media.

children.title: Children's Privacy
children.body: TuneSync does not knowingly collect data from children. The app does not require an account and does not collect personal information.

rights.title: Your Rights
rights.body: You can manage sources, library data, caches, and recordings inside the app. Uninstalling removes the app-container data; removing a source deletes its associated Keychain credentials. Data received by third-party providers is governed by their own privacy policies.

changes.title: Changes to This Policy
changes.body: We may update this privacy policy from time to time. Any changes will be posted here with an updated date.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: If you have questions about this privacy policy, contact us at:

support.title: Support
support.subtitle: We're here to help. Get answers to common questions or reach out to us.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: How do I add music to TuneSync?
faq.a1: TuneSync works with your own library. Import a local folder; connect WebDAV, SMB, FTP, NFS, or Synology DSM; or sync Plex, Jellyfin, Emby, Navidrome, Subsonic, and Audio Station. Open Settings → Library Sources & Indexing to add one.
faq.q2: Does TuneSync require an internet connection?
faq.a2: Music already on the device and cached content can play offline. Remote streaming, sync, and online metadata require a network. Cellular and Low Data Mode automatically limit work to lightweight lookups; artwork, AI, BPM, and audio analysis can wait for Wi-Fi.
faq.q3: How does the karaoke/sing mode work?
faq.a3: While a song plays, open Karaoke. TuneSync first separates the track into vocal and accompaniment stems on-device. Once ready, adjust the original-vocal level and record. Takes stay local and can be trimmed, shaped, and shared non-destructively in Recording Studio.
faq.a4: Yes. TuneSync is local-first and does not collect your personal data. See our Privacy Policy for details.
faq.a5: TuneSync 1.0.10 requires iOS 26.0 or later and is currently delivered as a native iPhone app.

resources.title: Documentation
resources.body: Browse our documentation for detailed guides on every feature.
